steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Data analysis means identifying patterns, trends, and relationships in your data. It involves describing what the data shows, calculating statistics, and explaining the geographical reasons behind the patterns you find.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of data, eliminating the influence of outliers. It is calculated as Q3 − Q1, where Q1 is the 25th percentile and Q3 is the 75th percentile.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Spearman's Rank measures the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables. It produces a value between -1 and +1. This is the most important statistical test for GCSE Geography fieldwork.

steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: To determine if your Spearman's Rank result is statistically significant (not just due to chance), compare your calculated rs value to the critical value table at the 95% confidence level (p = 0.05). If your calculated value exceeds the critical value, the result is significant and you can reject the null hypothesis.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know how to calculate and interpret Spearman's Rank - it appears frequently on exams Always compare your calculated rs to the critical value to test significance When describing data, quote specific figures - don't just say "it increased" In conclusions, explicitly state "the hypothesis is supported/rejected" Evaluation questions are common - prepare by identifying specific limitations of your methods Higher mark questions: suggest specific improvements and explain how they would increase reliability or validity Remember: correlation does not equal causation Use statistical language: significant, correlation, anomaly, confidence level
